D016-D021_h001.question:
It’s been maybe… six months? It’s hard to pin down exactly, but it’s gotten more noticeable in that time.

A lot of it circles around food and my body. I’m constantly doing mental math about what I’ve eaten, how many calories are in things, replaying meals in my head. If I eat something I didn’t plan, I can’t stop ruminating about it, like I’ve done something wrong. I’ll rewrite menus in my head, compare portions, look up nutrition facts over and over. I weigh myself more than I’d like to admit, and if the number isn’t “right,” it sets off this spiral of guilt and planning how to “fix” it.

At the same time, my mind throws up these really disturbing images or ideas that feel completely out of character—violent thoughts about hurting someone close to me, or really graphic sexual or religious stuff. They just pop in when I’m doing ordinary things, like interviewing someone or cooking, and they make me feel ashamed and unsettled.

I’ve also started washing my hands and re-cleaning the kitchen more than before, especially around food—cutting boards, counters, dishes—sometimes repeating it because I’m not sure it’s “clean enough.” It’s not taking over my whole day, but it’s starting to interfere with work and family routines.

A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Binge-Eating Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D016-D021_h002.question:

If something looks “off” on the tray, I feel this weird surge of anxiety until I fix it. I weigh myself more than I probably should, and I get stuck going over what I ate, how much I moved during a shift, whether I “deserve” to eat.

On top of that, I get these really disturbing thoughts out of nowhere—like suddenly imagining harming a patient or doing something sexually inappropriate at work, or even saying something blasphemous in front of a family. I would never do those things, but the images pop in and then I’m stuck replaying them, feeling guilty and kind of sick. Sometimes I’ll straighten equipment or line up medication vials just right, like if I get everything in order it’ll somehow neutralize those thoughts or calm me down enough to keep going.

    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D016-D021_h024.question:
I’ve been a flight attendant for about ten years, so I’m used to things needing to be neat, but over the past few months it feels like it’s getting out of hand. I get really stuck on how things are lined up—like the drink carts, the snack boxes, even the sugar packets in the galley.
